Subject: ACME — Post-call: model routing & integration next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sam — really helpful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Goals from the call
- Route different query types to model variants (LLM-large for complex generation, LLM-small for short completions, reranker/embedding pipeline for semantic search).
- Enforce latency SLOs for interactive UX (95p < 400ms for short requests) while controlling per-token cost for high-throughput workflows.
- Region-aware routing for EU/US data residency.

2) Integration notes (high level)
- SDK: we recommend starting with the Redwood JS SDK (examples below) and using API-keys scoped to project + role.
- Auth: support for customer KMS-backed keys and per-route tokens; we can demo short-lived tokens for browser clients.
- Structured output/tool calling: use the function-calling surface to limit hallucination and map outputs to your internal actions.
- Embeddings/reranker: pipeline idea — embed candidate set in batch, use fast ANN index (we can recommend vector DBs), then use reranker model variant for final scoring.

3) Model routing & policy (what we discussed)
- Primary policy: route by request type tag (e.g., "chat", "qa", "summarize") to model variants.
- Latency policy: if median latency > threshold or peak load detected, automatically failover to smaller model variant; optionally serve degraded but faster responses.
- Cost policy: for high-volume non-interactive requests (batch summarization) prefer quantized variants or server-side batching windows.
- Fallback chain: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> cached prefix response -> explicit error with graceful UX message.

4) Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with Dev and Marcus to walk SDK auth, sample routing policy, and the infra requirements (30–45m).
- Share a short example routing policy and architecture diagram (attached).
- Draft a mutual action plan + timing so we can scope Dedicated vs Hosted for first POC.

Action owner: Dev to run tech deep-dive; Marissa to schedule commercial follow-up.

Attachments: architecture_diagram_v2.pdf (PDF) attached — contains suggested deployment topology and region routing examples.

Thanks,

Thanks Sam — great questions. High-level answers and an example routing snippet below. Happy to cover in the deep-dive.

Auth/rotation
- We support short-lived tokens that can be minted by your Vault via our token-exchange endpoint (OAuth2 client credentials + signed assertion). We'll send a reference integration pattern (HashiCorp Vault -> Redwood token service) in the Drive folder.

Reranker latency
- Inline reranker adds ~60–150ms median depending on model size and candidate count; we typically recommend async reranking for paginated search UX and inline rerank for small candidate sets (<50). For strict tail latency SLOs we use a fallback policy to avoid blocking the main response.

Example routing policy (redwood_routing_policy.yaml attached):
- routes:
  - name: chat_interactive
    tags: [chat, interactive]
    primary_model: rwd-llm-large-v1
    fallback_chain: [rwd-llm-medium-v1, rwd-llm-small-quant-v1]
    latency_slo_ms: 400
    cost_priority: low
    region_policy: 
      eu: rwd-llm-eu-medium-v1
      us: rwd-llm-us-large-v1
  - name: semantic_search
    tags: [search, semantic]
    pipeline: [embedding_service, ann_index, reranker]
    reranker_model: rwd-rerank-small-v1
    reranker_inline_threshold: 40
    cost_priority: medium

Policy notes:
- The platform supports per-route token scopes and Key Management Service (KMS) integration if you want customer-managed keys.
- You can configure automated fallback thresholds: e.g., if p95 latency > latency_slo_ms for a sliding minute -> switch to next model in fallback_chain for 60s, notify via webhook.
- Region routing is policy-first: requests carry a routing attribute (country/region) and we map to model variants deployed in that region. If local capacity is constrained, we can failover to a compatible model in another region following your data residency guardrails.

Attachments: redwood_routing_policy.yaml (sample). Also added a simple SDK example to the Drive link showing short-lived token flow and function-calling for structured output.
